titulo: Seven Things You Let Slide Because This Week Does Not Count
caption:
Seven Things You Let Slide Because This Week Does Not Count

Cella is a small black rectangle with a crown, and she is letting seven things slide in the week that does not count. YouTube long video, 16:9. No Short and no Reel in this package.
descripcion:
NAOS. Choose friction.

The week from the twenty-fifth to the first has no deadlines, so a message, a favor, a borrowed thing, a vague yes, a decision, a list item and a small apology all slide. Cella goes through the seven, what each one costs the person on the other end, and a fix that takes ten minutes. Where there is a study it goes on the record; the rest is Cella's opinion. For whoever is holding something for January.

What the research says (so you can check us):
Masicampo EJ, Baumeister RF. (2011). Consider it done! Plan making can eliminate the cognitive effects of unfulfilled goals. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 101(4), 667-683. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0024192

The voice describes this single study as: unfinished goals kept intruding on thoughts during unrelated tasks, and writing a specific plan made those intrusions go away in the study.

#selfawareness #habits #NAOS
alt: A 8-minute video in 16:9 about seven things that slide in the week from Christmas to New Year. Cella, a small blocky black figure with two round white eyes and a crown, stands in colored rooms while on-screen cards give each thing: the message, the favor, the borrowed thing, the vague yes, the decision, the list and the apology. Each part says it does not count this week, shows what the person on the other end is waiting for, and ends with a ten-minute fix on a three-row card. One study, Masicampo and Baumeister 2011, appears with an ON THE RECORD stamp; everything else is Cella's opinion. In the last part a 30-second clock runs while Cella waits for the oldest of the seven to be written on a scrap of paper with a date. The thumbnail shows Cella large with a red crown on an amber field, the words This week does not count, and a big 7 on a calendar card.
